correctness.rationale: Direct 2x2 inversion and characteristic polynomial produce trace t>0, det d>0 and discriminant Δ; positive-real and conjugate cases give necessary and sufficient spectral radius<1. Matrix-power necessity excludes all q>=2c. The standalone checker passed 50,139 checks including rational square-zero, without replacing the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2D primal--dual KKT model is a motivated minimal test of skew-resolvent splitting. The all-parameter sharp stability/rate classification and exact q<2c cutoff yield a nontrivial design principle for finite universal termination, with a substantial relaxation beyond generic sufficient bounds in an open parameter region. It is more than a single arbitrary special-case computation and is useful as a precisely calibrated numerical benchmark. It does not promise robustness, scaling or Halpern/ADMM performance.
